To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the COPD Assessment Test is an eight-question, patient-completed quality-of-life questionnaire that is easy to administer; the COPD Assessment test is a valid, reliable and sensitive measure of change in health status in response to pulmonary rehabilitation; the minimum clinically important change for the COPD Assessment score is 2.9 points.
the CAT score is a simple to use, patient-completed quality-of-life instrument that contains eight items covering the impact of COPD symptoms.

the COPD Assessment Test (CAT) is an outcome measure that can be easily implemented in clinical pulmonary rehabilitation (COPD) programmes, that the CAT score improves in response to rehabilitation and that the CAT score can distinguish categories of improvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel, patient-reported, outcome measure, the CAT, for use in COPD and other respiratory conditions.
the role of physical activity in health.
the development, evaluation, and implementation of new and existing interventions for the treatment and management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAT score is a valid, simple to use quality of life instrument in patients with COPD and that it is responsive to change following PR.
the CAT is a simple and valid tool to assess the impact of COPD symptoms on health status, and that the minimum important difference is 2.9 points, but this is not a robust conclusion.
a change in CAT score of 3.5 is the minimum clinically important change in the CAT score.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CAT score is a valid and responsive measure of change in COPD quality of life in response to PR.
the CAT is a useful measure for the assessment and monitoring of patients with COPD.
the CAT score is a valid measure of response to PR in COPD and can distinguish between categories of response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAT score can be used in PR programmes and can be used to identify those individuals who are not benefiting from PR.
the CAT is a simple, quick to administer, valid, reliable and responsive outcome measure.
the CAT is a simple, easy to use, patient-completed measure that is responsive to clinical change and can distinguish between categories of response to PR.
